sources.post_title: On breadth vs. depth in learning
sources.title: 2023-10-26 Patreon letter - On breadth vs. depth in learning
sources.summary: Reading broadly helps identify worthwhile questions and sources; deep study becomes appropriate as those questions sharpen. Matuschak treats curiosity, personal meaning, and available energy as central to choosing a reading pace. He distinguishes the relatively small cost of reviewing memory prompts from the greater effort of writing them, and warns that emotionally irrelevant prompts can undermine a review practice. Hands-on projects and conceptual study can support each other when gaps are identified and addressed.

sources.title: 2023-09-30 Patreon letter - Highlight-driven practice and comprehension support
2023-08-31 Patreon letter - Studying myself studying linear algebra
sources.summary: Matuschak studies linear algebra to examine the limits of his own reading strategies, memory prompts, and problem-solving practice. Writing prompts encourages attention, but it can also produce shallow paraphrases, miss difficult ideas, or create unwanted review commitments. Problem sets help reveal comprehension gaps, yet they do not necessarily identify the missing explanation or test every conceptual detail. The experiment motivates more direct support for detecting and resolving misunderstandings while learning.

sources.title: 2023-08-01 Patreon letter - Initial experiments in self-explanation support
sources.summary: The letter distinguishes a representation of a text's literal statements from an understanding connected to prior knowledge and inferred relationships. Self-explanation can strengthen those connections and reveal comprehension gaps. Matuschak experiments with passage-linked explanations, visual feedback, and language-model feedback, but finds that compulsory explanation can feel burdensome. He seeks reading interactions that encourage effective comprehension strategies while producing something the reader values beyond the immediate exercise.

sources.title: 2023-06-30 Patreon letter - Reading comprehension and memory systems
2023-05-31 Patreon letter - Fluid practice for fluid understanding
2023-03-31 Patreon letter - Memory systems and problem-solving practice
sources.summary: Remembering definitions and equations does not guarantee the ability to solve unfamiliar problems. Following a physics learner, Matuschak examines how practice must engage the processes needed in real use, help learners develop adaptable problem-solving patterns, and expose unnoticed comprehension gaps. The letter asks how memory practice, varied exercises, and conversation can work together to produce usable understanding rather than accurate repetition alone.

sources.title: 2023-02-28 Patreon letter - Becoming a Wizard-of-Oz learning assistant
sources.summary: Matuschak becomes a learning assistant for an adult pursuing a demanding physics project. Tutoring recordings and narrated review sessions reveal confusion, motivation, and weaknesses that interviews alone had missed. He writes and revises prompts in response, connecting them to the learner's meaningful experiences. The experiment explores close collaboration as a way to discover better learning tools, with practical feedback shaping both the prompts and the surrounding system.

sources.post_title: Towards impact through intimacy in my memory system research
sources.title: 2022-12-27 Patreon letter - Towards impact through intimacy in my memory system research
sources.summary: Matuschak redirects his memory-system research toward the depth and usefulness of understanding. Broad adoption and improved recall scores do not by themselves establish that people can use what they learn. He proposes close work with a few committed learners, including coaching, diaries, and bespoke interventions. The aim is to observe cognitive and emotional changes in detail and discover promising design principles before pursuing broader evaluation or scale.

sources.post_title: Lessons from summer 2022’s mnemonic medium prototype
sources.title: 2022-10-14 Patreon letter - Lessons from summer 2022’s mnemonic medium prototype
sources.summary: Observing a new mnemonic-medium prototype reveals how much outcomes depend on readers' aims and prior familiarity with spaced repetition. Margin prompts can guide attention, but they also encourage distracted or compulsory prompt-reading. Some readers want to mark an important idea without immediately committing to repeated practice. Matuschak explores more flexible reading interactions, distinguishing attention, expression, and tentative interest from the stronger decision to save a memory prompt.

sources.post_title: The joyful surprises of user observation
sources.title: 2022-06-30 Patreon letter - The joyful surprises of user observation
sources.summary: Live observation shows that a prototype can change readers' behavior in ways its designer did not anticipate. Matuschak argues for lightweight experiments and an open-ended stance toward discovering new needs. Readers sometimes use memory prompts as summaries or navigation aids, and many dislike sustained reading on a computer. These observations reshape the design problem beyond checking whether the original feature works as intended.

sources.post_title: Exponentials and forgetting in Quantum Country
sources.title: 2022-02-28 Patreon letter - Exponentials and forgetting in Quantum Country
sources.summary: The letter revisits Quantum Country's memory data and the possibility that additional practice yields large increases in retention time. It separates durable recall, review cost, forgetting without practice, and transfer into real-world understanding as different questions. Unexpectedly slow forgetting complicates interpretation of the experiments. Matuschak presents the analysis as preliminary and emphasizes that improved recall alone does not establish deeper understanding or practical ability.

sources.post_title: Quantum Country’s suspiciously flat forgetting curves
sources.title: 2021-11-30 Patreon letter - Quantum Country’s suspiciously flat forgetting curves
sources.summary: Quantum Country experiments show unexpectedly little decline in recall across some delays, making conventional forgetting-curve interpretations difficult. Matuschak investigates differences among questions and considers whether the wording of prompts supplies cues that inflate apparent retention. He cautions that these preliminary results may not generalize to other memory systems. The central research problem is explaining the measurements before using them to justify changes in review scheduling.

sources.post_title: Architectures for a more flexible mnemonic medium
sources.title: 2021-09-30 Patreon letter - Architectures for a more flexible mnemonic medium
sources.summary: The proposed mnemonic-medium architecture supports different reading situations without forcing everyone through the same sequence. Readers should be able to select, edit, and create prompts using representations shared with the author's prompts. Matuschak explores compact lists, contextual interactions, and optional review at section breaks. The design aims to preserve guided learning where useful while accommodating selective reading, personal connections, and changes made during later review.

sources.post_title: Revamping the mnemonic medium around reader control
sources.title: 2021-08-24 Patreon letter - Revamping the mnemonic medium around reader control
sources.summary: Early mnemonic texts make the author's chosen prompts dominate the reading experience. Matuschak argues that readers need more fundamental control over what they study, how they express it, and which personal connections they record. Editing or deleting assigned prompts alone does not resolve the underlying imbalance. He proposes treating author-written prompts as adaptable material within the reader's own learning practice, with fluid opportunities to select and create.

sources.title: 2021-03-25 Patreon letter - Too easy to be effortless
sources.summary: A memory system can achieve high recall while still making practice feel tedious. Matuschak distinguishes a feeling of effortless engagement from tasks that are merely easy. Quantum Country's often trivial reviews motivate questions about boredom, appropriate challenge, and the emotional experience of maintenance practice. Scheduling and other optimizations matter insofar as they help the system feel more closely connected to the learner's intentions.

sources.title: 2021-02-02 Patreon letter - In search of better questions
sources.summary: Accumulating memory data is useful only when research questions can produce meaningful new understanding. Matuschak challenges vague evaluations of whether a system works and narrow studies concerned only with memorization. He seeks questions about how reading tools change learning, feeling, and action. The letter treats choosing the right questions and collecting the corresponding evidence as prerequisites for inventing more powerful learning environments.

sources.post_title: The carrying capacity of a regular memory practice; deliberate practice and flow
sources.title: 2020-09-30 Patreon letter - The carrying capacity of a regular memory practice; deliberate practice and flow
sources.summary: A regular memory practice could gradually support a substantial body of knowledge, but review capacity is only part of the problem. Writing effective prompts about conceptual material requires considerable skill and effort. Matuschak explores how expert-written prompts embedded in explanations might reduce that burden while retaining meaningful context. The value of the practice depends on reinforcing ideas that matter to the learner rather than accumulating disconnected trivia.
